task.description: WF-03 Step 10: independently re-derive, from the actual shipped code and a self-run test suite, whether ISS-0226's 4 acceptance criteria are genuinely met. Not a report-copy of TEST-RUNNER's step-09.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: worker result has an explicit closed type (struct or tagged tuple set) declared in lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex
AC2: handle_info/2 is total over that type -- an unrecognised shape is handled, not a function-clause crash
AC3: a test drives an unexpected run_op/1 return and asserts the pool survives with slot bookkeeping intact
AC4: no change to ISS-0224 invariants INV-SP-A1..A3 or the owner-monitor reclaim semantics

result.summary:
Independently re-verified all 4 ACs against commit 2c53c11 on fix/WF03-ISS0226-20260822.

AC1/AC2 -- read `git show b37941d -- lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex` directly. `@typep worker_result :: provision_result() | drop_result()` (provision_result/drop_result each a closed 2-member tagged-tuple set) is a genuinely closed type. `classify_worker_result/2` has exactly 4 exact-match clauses plus a final `defp classify_worker_result(_op, _result), do: :invalid` catch-all, and `handle_info/2`'s clause A branches on `{:ok, validated_result}` vs `:invalid`, routing the latter to `handle_worker_death/1` -- total over the callback's actual input domain, no possible FunctionClauseError path remains. CONFIRMED.

AC3 -- read test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs lines 1196-1309 directly: both new tests use `:sys.replace_state/2` to inject a real in_flight op then `send(pool, {fake_task_ref, :not_a_recognized_shape})` against the live GenServer, asserting `Process.alive?(pool)`, in_flight recovery via the drain/nil check, and (for the :drop case) the blocked caller receiving `{:error, :release_failed}`. Beyond reading, I ran my OWN independent mutation: commented out the catch-all clause in lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex, re-ran `mix test test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs` -- exactly the 2 ISS-0226 regression tests failed, both with the exact FunctionClauseError in classify_worker_result/2 the fix exists to prevent (confirmed via the raised stacktrace), all other 16 tests unaffected. Reverted the mutation, re-ran: 18/18 clean, `git diff --stat` empty confirming exact restoration. This is independent (not TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's mutation re-read) and demonstrates genuine discrimination. CONFIRMED.

AC4 -- read the diff's hunk line ranges (`git diff 09fd3b0~1 2c53c11 -- lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex`): 5 hunks, header line ranges topping out at 592-631. Grepped current file for `complete_op/3` (674-736), `handle_worker_death/1` (745+), and the `:DOWN` clause B handler (461) -- all three are at line numbers strictly outside every changed hunk's range. No edit touches them. CONFIRMED untouched.

Full-suite re-run (own, not copied from step-09): `TEST_PARALLEL_N=16` (host default) produced 2 different flaky outcomes across 2 attempts -- run 1: 3 failures (Context.scoped_repo_opts/1 arity assertion, EngineConcurrencyTest timing ratio, and one sandbox_pool RT-6 schema-drop-timing check); run 2: 2 partitions aborted entirely with `could not create hard link ... permission denied` (Windows Mix build-lock contention, 0 tests run in those partitions). None of the 3 run-1 failures reproduced test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs in 5 consecutive isolated re-runs (18/18 clean every time, including immediately after the mutation revert) -- confirmed these are host-level resource-contention artifacts of 16-way parallelism on this Windows machine, not code regressions (RT-6 predates ISS-0226 and is unrelated to the two new tests). Reduced to `TEST_PARALLEL_N=6` (avoids the hardlink contention) and got a clean run: combined 1547 tests, 5 properties, 0 failures (1552/1552 passed) -- matching TEST-RUNNER's step-09 count exactly, independently re-derived rather than trusted.

All 4 ACs independently confirmed met. No new decision-record conflicts; docs/migration/decisions/ not implicated (this is a bugfix, not a stage gate).
issues: Full-suite runs at this host's default TEST_PARALLEL_N=16 are unreliable (Windows Mix build-directory hard-link lock contention aborts partitions outright, and separately produces transient timing-based test failures unrelated to any single change) -- worth filing as its own infra issue so future TEST-RUNNER/RELEASE-VALIDATOR runs default to a lower N on this host rather than rediscovering this each time.
